name: HighLevel
blurb: CRM contacts and conversations for agencies
headline: Moderate: a private app works same day for 5 agencies; more needs a public review (10 business days per changelog).

firstTest.text: Same day for a private app installed in your own agency or sub-account. Private apps go live with no review.

production.text: Private apps allow 5 agencies; at 6, installs are blocked until you go public or pass a Security Review. Public apps need Marketplace approval.

approvalWait.text: None for private apps. Public apps: a 2023 changelog says 10 business days, a third-party guide says 7 to 14. Current guidelines give no timeline.

whoCanRegister.text: Anyone can create an app. Public listing needs review and a Loom demo. OAuth needs Advanced API access, on the Agency Pro plan.

testMode.text: Private apps allow 5 agencies (made since 18 Nov 2025). Limits: 100 requests per 10 seconds, 200,000 a day. Access lasts 24 hours.

steps.title: Sign up as a developer
steps.detail: Go to the HighLevel Marketplace and sign in to your developer account. Signup steps and cost weren't documented on the pages I opened.

steps.title: Create a private app
steps.detail: Go to 'My Apps', then 'Create App', and fill in the name, type, target user, who can install and listing type. HighLevel suggests Sub-account as target user, 'Both Agency and Sub-account' for installs, and starting Private.

steps.title: Set scopes and redirect address
steps.detail: In 'Advanced Settings', then 'Auth', add the fewest scopes and an HTTPS redirect address that matches your flow exactly. Create a client key and copy the Client Secret right away; it isn't shown again.

steps.title: Build the install flow
steps.detail: An admin opens your Installation URL and picks an account, then HighLevel sends them to your redirect address with a one-time code. Swap that code for tokens on your server.

steps.title: Store and rotate tokens
steps.detail: Save the access token (about 24 hours), refresh token (up to a year), token type and agency or location ID. A refresh token works once and returns a new one, so save each new one.

steps.title: Handle agency and location tokens
steps.detail: An agency token runs agency APIs; a location token runs sub-account APIs. To act on one sub-account with an agency token, request a location token with your agency and location IDs.

steps.title: Respect rate limits
steps.detail: Limits are 100 requests per 10 seconds and 200,000 per day, per app and per sub-account or agency. Read the rate limit headers instead of counting yourself.

steps.title: Test real installs
steps.detail: Install the private app into test sub-accounts. The cap counts agencies, not sub-accounts: you see a warning at 4 to 5, and installs are blocked at 6.

steps.title: Prepare listing and demo
steps.detail: Write the name, description, costs and setup needs, and add real screenshots and a support email or phone. The Loom demo is the last submission step: show install, setup, main function, the third-party connection, errors, and uninstall.

steps.title: Go public and submit
steps.detail: Switch to Public and submit to Marketplace review; updates go live only after approval. If rejected, you get the reasons; fix them and resubmit. Only one Draft or Disapproved version can exist at a time.
steps.time: 1 hr to submit, then review wait

blockers.title: Private app stops taking installs at the sixth agency
blockers.fix: Private apps made since 18 November 2025 allow 5 agencies. Go public, or request a Security Review with a demo video, a scopes-justification video and a written reason the app must stay private.

blockers.title: Review rejects you for too many scopes
blockers.fix: Request only scopes you use and be ready to justify each one. A third-party guide calls over-requesting the top cause of rejection, and HighLevel's guidelines list it as a reason to reject.

blockers.title: Review rejects HighLevel branding
blockers.fix: Don't use HighLevel or GHL logos without authorization. Unofficial integrations need a visible disclaimer, white-label apps must show no HighLevel branding, and listing text should avoid 'sub-account' and 'agency'.

blockers.title: Review says your demo doesn't match the app
blockers.fix: Core functionality must be complete and testable in the submitted version, with no undocumented setup. Re-record the Loom if the app or flow changed.

blockers.title: Refresh token lost after a failed refresh
blockers.fix: A refresh token stops working once used. Save the new one atomically, and lock the refresh so two workers don't use the same token.

blockers.title: A busy sub-account hits limits
blockers.fix: Limits are 100 per 10 seconds and 200,000 per day for each app and sub-account. Queue calls and slow down when the remaining-requests header runs low.

agentCan: Write the install redirect, code swap and token refresh with safe rotation
Turn an agency token into a location token for a chosen sub-account
Queue API calls under the burst and daily limits using the rate limit headers
Draft the listing copy, scope justifications and Loom script
Check the app against the review guidelines before you submit
youDo: Create the developer account and the app, and copy the client secret
Install the app into a test sub-account and sign in as an admin
Record the Loom demo and submit the app for review
Provide a support email or phone and legal pages if asked
Verify your domain and identity if HighLevel requests it

drafts.title: Listing description
drafts.body: [Product name] is an AI assistant for [agency or business type]. It connects to your HighLevel sub-account to [read and create contacts / reply to conversations / book appointments]. You approve access when you install, and you can uninstall at any time. Requires: [your own account, plan, any cost]. Setup takes about [N] minutes. Support: [email]. This app is not affiliated with or endorsed by HighLevel.

drafts.title: Loom demo script
drafts.body: 1. Show the install from the Installation URL and pick a sub-account. 2. Show setup in our app. 3. Run the main task, for example: ask the assistant to add a contact and show it in HighLevel. 4. Show what happens if the user denies access or a call fails. 5. Show disconnect and uninstall, and say what data we delete. Keep it short and narrate each step.

drafts.title: Scope justification
drafts.body: contacts.write: creates contacts the user asks the assistant to add. contacts.readonly: finds an existing contact before creating a duplicate. conversations/message.write: sends a reply the user approved. We do not request any scope we do not use, and we do not store HighLevel data after uninstall.

unconfirmed: The current public review wait. The 10 business days is from a 2023 changelog post. The 7 to 14 business day range is a third-party blog. The current guidelines page gives no timeline.
How developer account signup works and whether it costs anything. The pages I opened do not say.
Whether the Agency Pro plan requirement for OAuth applies to you as the developer, to installing users, or both. The help centre says OAuth needs Advanced API access on Agency Pro.
Whether reviewers get test credentials. The guidelines only require the Loom demo and a complete, testable app.
What response a rate-limited call gets. The rate limit page lists headers but does not describe a 429 reply.
Whether private apps created before 18 November 2025 have any cap. The policy covers apps created on or after that date.
The access token lifetime is stated as 86,399 or 86,400 seconds in the two samples, so 'about 24 hours' is used.
